newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Channel 5 wins 2.8 pct Q2 audience shr.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Channel 5 wins 2.8 pct Q2 audience shr.

text.p: Britain's Channel 5, the country's newest terrestrial television channel, attracted almost three percent of the UK television viewing audience in the second quarter of 1997, an advertising trade group said on Wednesday.

The Institute of Practitioners in Advertising (IPA) said Channel 5, was launched in late March as Britain's third commercial terrestrial station, won 2.8 percent of the total television viewing audience and 4.9 percent of the commercial viewing audience.

"Channel 5 shows a bias towards the young and downmarket viewers in its share, and usefully shows a higher share in the important peak viewing hours," the IPA said in its quarterly report, "Trends in Television Viewing."
In June, when Channel 5 had an average weekly audience share of 2.7 percent, the station said it was on course to meet its target of a five percent TV audience share by the end of this year.

The ITV, Britain's largest commercial television network, continued to lose audience share in the second quarter, falling to 32.2 percent of the total viewing audience from 34.3 percent in the first quarter and 34.4 percent in the 1996 second quarter, the IPA said.

BBC1, the flagship station of the state-run BBC, also lost audience share in the second quarter, falling to 30.9 percent from 31.8 percent in the 1997 first quarter and 32.2 percent in the 1996 second quarter, the Institute said.

Channel 4, the commercial, state-controlled station, saw audience share slip to 10.7 percent in the second quarter from 10.8 percent in the first quarter of this year. But it remained ahead of the 10.6 percent share it won in the 1996 second quarter, the IPA said.

Britain's cable and satellite channels, meanwhile, gained market share, rising to an 11.8 percent share of the total audience in the second quarter, compared to 11.4 percent in the 1997 first quarter and 9.9 percent in the 1997 second quarter, the IPA said.
